title: fix(verify-lock): a resumed slot keeps its place through its second wait
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ82EQnMDeFFkR9nnNXYvhRv9)_

Fixes #36532

## What changes

`scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` only (plus its `--self-test`):

- **A resumed slot is aged from its resume, not from its first arrival.** The queue order is the ticket's *filename* prefix; the record's third field is only read by the waiter-age bound (`TICKET_MAX_AGE_S` = 840 s). `take_ticket` used to write the ORIGINAL arrival back into that field on resume, so a resumer read as over-age ~300 s into its second 540 s wait. The next scan (its own, or any sibling's) deleted the ticket, and the caller was re-minted at the back of the queue. On resume the field now holds the resume time, and the file (the place) is kept unchanged.
- This also holds against an older copy of the script in a sibling worktree. All copies share the queue directory, and every copy already ages a live ticket from that field.
- `ticket_arrival_s` reads the original arrival back from the filename. The resume log line and `--status`'s `parked N: … place kept Ns` line use it, so they still report the age of the place.
- **The exit-99 note only promises "Your place is KEPT" when a ticket exists to park.** If the ticket was removed mid-wait, or the queue was unusable, it now says the place was LOST and that the next call starts at the back. That was the second reading on the card: the promise was not honoured.

## Why

Both readings on the card are the same defect. A dev waited through 12 budgets (~108 min) without acquiring, while first-budget arrivals won. The second reading came from a head-of-queue caller: it sits inside `flock` and never re-scans, so siblings pruned its ticket and its "KEPT" place was gone on the next call.

## Verification

Nine new self-test cases sit between the #12538 ageing block and the #15581 headship block. One uses a parked fixture whose arrival is already past `TICKET_MAX_AGE_S`, resumed for real behind a holder. Another removes a waiting slot's ticket by hand. A further in-process pair checks that the resumed record reads `active` and keeps its filename.

- Red without the fix: the new battery spliced onto `main`'s code fails 5 of the new cases (same place, `--status` arrival, filename kept, KEPT not promised, LOST said). The other failures in that hybrid run come from running it outside the repo, not from these cases.
- Green with the fix: `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --self-test`, 266 ✓, 0 ✗.
- `dispatch-gates --commands scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`: 28 derived commands. 27 exit 0 (including `check:bash32-floor`, `check:self-test-wired`, `check:self-test-workflow-commands`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`). NOT MEASURED: `check:type-check-debt`, reason: it hit the 280 s local cap (exit 124). It ratchets the TypeScript ledger and this diff touches no TypeScript; CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- Not run locally: lint farm and type-check lanes. CI runs them; the diff touches no package.
